# FulcrumGrid — full text for LLMs
> FulcrumGrid is a family of purpose-built business apps for small and mid-sized businesses — Command Center (real-time operations dashboard), Collection (accounts receivable and payments), and HR Suite (people operations) — plus custom business apps built on the same secure, auditable platform. The apps share one consistent experience; you can start with one and add more as you grow. FulcrumGrid is fully bilingual (English and Arabic/RTL) and is built by Avenlor Consulting. Contact: contact@avenlorconsulting.com.
This file inlines the readable content of FulcrumGrid's core pages (English and Arabic) in one place. Index with links: https://fulcrumgrid.com/llms.txt · Full page list: https://fulcrumgrid.com/sitemap.xml

## Command Center
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/command-center/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Operations · Available now

# See everything. Control anything.

Command Center is your business's control room — a real-time dashboard that brings your key metrics, workflows, and alerts into one view, so nothing slips and every decision is made on live data.

Request a demo Open Command Center All products

01 · Pricing

## Command Center pricing.

Flat monthly price per organization (Pilot plan). 14-day free trial, no card required.

#### Command Center

Per organization / month

Pilot SAR 490

Flat monthly price per organization. 14-day free trial, no card required.

#### Included

On the Pilot plan

Live KPIs & custom dashboards ✓

Alerts & automated workflows ✓

Reporting & exports ✓

Email support ✓

Start free trial See full pricing ↗

02 · Capabilities

## Everything you need to run operations live.

From high-level health to the single alert that needs attention right now.

#### Live dashboards

Build dashboards from any data on the grid. Metrics refresh in real time — no exports, no stale reports.

#### Alerts & thresholds

Set thresholds on any metric and get notified the moment they're crossed — in-app, by email, or to your team channel.

#### Automated workflows

Turn a signal into an action: open a task, notify an owner, or trigger a job in another app — automatically.

#### Reporting & exports

Build the reports your team needs and export them anytime — no more digging through a dozen spreadsheets.

#### Custom views & KPIs

Define the KPIs that matter to your business and pin them into role-specific views for each team.

#### Goals, tasks & approvals

OKRs, KPIs and projects with the tasks beneath them — subtasks, dependencies and a kanban board — plus an approvals workflow so decisions get signed off on the record. Import KPI actuals and tasks in bulk from CSV, with a preview before you commit.

#### Business cards

Capture the business cards your team collects — scanned, categorized and searchable, so new contacts never get lost.

#### Ask your data with AI

Ask about your operations and finances in plain language and get an answer built only from a tenant-isolated snapshot of your own data — the model never touches the database, so nothing crosses org boundaries. Off until you turn it on.

#### Auto-summaries & anomaly alerts

Plain-language summaries of your dashboards, tasks and finances, plus anomaly detection that flags unusual KPI movements and outliers in uploaded trial balances before they become a problem.

#### Audit trail

Every change, alert, and action is logged. Know what happened, when, and who acted on it.

03 · Integrations

## Connects to your ERP and accounting.

Feed live balances into your dashboards without double entry. All integrations →

#### SAP Business One

Two-way sync for business partners, items and journal entries — no re-keying, and balances land straight in Command Center.

#### Odoo

A two-way connector that keeps contacts, invoices and payments in step between Odoo and the grid.

#### Oracle

Stream live balances and receivables from Oracle financials into your dashboards and alerts.

#### QuickBooks Online

Link QuickBooks Online (QBO) to match invoices to payments and reconcile automatically.

#### Slack & Teams alerts

Post a summary of overdue items and key events to a Slack or Teams channel through an incoming webhook — so your team sees what needs attention without opening the app.

#### One connection on Growth

Growth includes a single ERP connection; Enterprise unlocks unlimited connections with a scheduled pull.

#### Scheduled pull

Let Command Center pull records from your ERP on a schedule, so dashboards stay current on their own.

#### REST API & developer tools

A versioned REST API (v1) over your finance and operational data, with API keys and a live/test sandbox, outbound webhooks, and an OpenAPI spec plus Postman collection on a developer guide — so your team can build on your own data.

#### Single sign-on (SSO)

Sign in through your own identity provider over OIDC, so access to Command Center follows your company directory.

04 · Built for

## Made for the people who keep things running.

#### Operations leads

Watch throughput, SLAs, and exceptions across the whole business without waiting on a weekly report.

#### Finance

Track cash, receivables, and spend live — and get alerted before a number becomes a problem.

#### Executives

One screen for the health of the company, with the ability to drill into any metric down to the record.

05 · Your region

## Built for your region.

GCC-native finance, Arabic-first, and multi-currency — Command Center adapts to your market.

#### Tax & Zakat

Tax and Zakat as a first-class group in your P&L and executive snapshot — GCC finance, out of the box.

#### VAT-ready

VAT tracked alongside your other liabilities, with a compliance and governance module to keep filings on track.

#### Arabic & multi-currency

Arabic, right-to-left throughout, with reporting in SAR, USD, EUR or your own currency.

#### Country-aware console

The console offers the right languages and a sensible default timezone for each market automatically.

06 · The FulcrumGrid family

## Collection
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/collection/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Finance · Available now

# Get paid, predictably.

Collection turns messy receivables into a clear, auditable process. Track every invoice, automate the follow-ups, offer payment plans, and reconcile the money coming in — so revenue lands on time and nothing falls through the cracks.

Request a demo Open Collection All products

01 · Pricing

## Collection pricing.

Starter is free — paid plans from SAR 450 / month.

#### Collection

Per workspace / month

Starter Free

Starter is free — paid plans from SAR 450 / month.

#### Included

On the Starter plan

Invoice & ledger tracking ✓

Automated reminders & plans ✓

Payment reconciliation ✓

Email support ✓

Start free trial See full pricing ↗

02 · Capabilities

## From invoice to paid, in one place.

Every step of the receivables cycle, tracked and automated.

#### Invoice & ledger tracking

A live view of every invoice — who owes what, since when, and where each one stands.

#### Automated reminders

Schedule polite, escalating follow-ups that reach each debtor on the channel they actually answer — sent automatically so no one has to chase manually.

#### Payment plans

Split a balance into scheduled installments and let Collection track each one to completion.

#### Payment reconciliation

Match incoming payments to invoices automatically and flag anything that doesn't line up.

#### Cheque register

Capture post-dated cheques against an account, track them through to cleared, and post the cleared cheque straight to your ERP — with capture and clearing kept as separate duties.

#### ERP connectors

Two-way sync with SAP Business One, Odoo, Oracle Fusion, Oracle Integration (OIC) and Daftra — collected payments and cleared cheques post to your ledger automatically, with a posting-activity feed for every connector.

#### Single sign-on (SSO)

Sign in through your own identity provider over OIDC, with just-in-time provisioning and a break-glass admin login, so access follows your company directory.

#### Aging & risk reports

See receivables by age bucket, spot at-risk accounts early, and forecast the cash that's actually coming.

#### Disputes & notes

Log disputes, promises to pay, and account notes against each record — a full history for every customer.

#### Field collection & visits

Dispatch field collectors by territory with geo-routed day plans, proof-of-visit (device GPS inside the debtor's geo-fence), conduct-hour and workplace limits, and cash hand-in reconciliation from collector to cashier — with collecting and reconciling kept as separate duties.

#### AI account brief

An AI read of any account in five short lines — balance, promises, disputes, risk — each citing the record it came from, so a collector gets the full picture in seconds.

#### Draft & structure with AI

Draft a collections message for a person to review and send, and turn a free-text call note into a structured outcome you confirm — the AI proposes, a human decides.

#### Private, governed AI

An opt-in add-on with your own AI key (Anthropic or OpenAI). Debtor identities are pseudonymised and personal data scrubbed before anything leaves — with a kill switch, supervisor review, and retention and erasure built in.

03 · Built for

## For everyone chasing revenue.

#### Accounts receivable

Work the whole book from one queue instead of a stack of spreadsheets and sticky notes.

#### Finance teams

Cut days-sales-outstanding and forecast cash with confidence backed by live data.

#### Growing businesses

Professional, consistent collections without hiring a whole department to run them.

04 · Your region

## Built for your region.

Multi-currency, Arabic-first, and privacy-ready — Collection works the way your market does.

#### Multi-currency

Receivables and payments carry their own ISO currency, so you collect in SAR, USD, EUR or any currency your customers pay in.

#### Arabic & debtor portal

Arabic, right-to-left throughout, including the self-service portal where debtors view balances and settle.

#### Privacy & data-subject rights

Built-in data-subject request handling helps you meet GDPR-style privacy obligations wherever you operate.

#### Jurisdiction-tagged legal

Tag each legal case with its jurisdiction, so escalations follow the rules of the market they belong to.

05 · The FulcrumGrid family

## Explore the rest of the grid.

## HR Suite
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/hr-suite/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

People · Available now

# People operations, handled.

HR Suite runs your team from hire to retire. Keep every employee record, onboard in a click, run payroll, track time and leave, and manage performance — all in one compliant, easy-to-run place.

Request a demo Open HR Suite All products

New · AI Copilot & Agents

## AI that works the way HR has to.

A copilot on every page, AI reviews grounded in the record, and acting agents that never move without a human approval — on the model and data boundary you choose.

#### Copilot on every page

Ask about any policy in plain language and get an answer drawn only from the policies you're allowed to see, cited to the source. If no policy covers it, it says so — it never guesses.

#### AI reviews, in context

A grounded summary right on the record — review an employee, summarize a candidate, explain a pay-run variance, triage attendance exceptions. Read-only: it summarizes, it never changes the record.

#### Acting agents, human-approved

Agents like AI shortlist propose a change; nothing happens until a person approves it in the Approvals inbox. Whoever ran the agent can't approve it — the same separation of duties as money.

#### Low-stakes steps only

Agents take only reversible, low-stakes steps such as a pipeline move. Money, employment status, ratings and government actions are never available to an AI agent.

#### Your model, your data

Try it on a capped shared key, bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Azure key, or point it at a self-hosted model so data never leaves your infrastructure. Keys are encrypted and isolated per tenant.

#### Governed & auditable

AI is off until you turn it on, gated by the Act with AI permission, with an Agent Center log of every request — metadata only, so it holds no employee data.

01 · Pricing

## HR Suite pricing.

Billed per active seat (Starter plan). 14-day free trial, no card required.

#### HR Suite

Per seat / month

Starter SAR 12

Core HR on the Starter plan. 14-day free trial, no card required.

Core HR & time off ✓

Expenses & HR letters ✓

News, recognition & probation ✓

Start free trial See full pricing ↗

02 · Capabilities

## The whole employee lifecycle.

One system for everything HR, from the offer letter onward.

#### Employee records

A single, secure profile for every employee — documents, roles, compensation, and history in one file.

#### Onboarding

Turn a new hire into a set-up teammate with checklists, e-signatures, and automatic account provisioning — plus AI-assisted import that maps your spreadsheet columns and reads existing documents to propose the setup for you to approve.

#### Payroll

Run accurate payroll on schedule, with earnings, deductions, and payslips generated for every cycle — including sales commissions recorded by your team and paid straight through the pay run.

#### Time & attendance

Clock-ins, timesheets, and shift tracking that flow straight into payroll — no double entry.

#### Leave management

Requests, approvals, and balances for every leave type — with a shared calendar the whole team can see.

#### Performance & reviews

Goals, feedback, and review cycles that keep growth conversations on track and on record.

#### Learning & development

Build courses, lessons and quizzes with completion certificates — or bring provider catalogues from Udemy Business, LinkedIn Learning and Coursera, assign them, track completions, and recommend them right inside reviews and development plans.

#### Company news

A company news feed with articles, reactions and moderated comments, alongside read-and-accept announcements — so the whole company stays current from the Home screen and the mobile app.

#### Approval workflows

Design multi-step approval chains with your own conditions — amount, department, grade — for leave, expenses, travel, offers and loans, with separation of duties built in.

#### Policy Library

Publish versioned policies and procedures; new hires read and acknowledge them automatically, with a full compliance audit trail.

#### Business travel

Trips, per-diems, advances and settlement — approved through a workflow and paid through expenses, with GCC home-leave air tickets.

#### Mobile & self-service

A mobile app for clock-in, requests and payslips — with approved-phone binding that stops buddy-punching.

#### Talent & hiring

A full ATS and public careers page, weighted AI CV scoring and an AI shortlist you approve, scorecards, one-way video interviews with AI transcription and evaluation, and live interview scheduling that books Google Meet, Teams or Zoom, offers and internal mobility — then performance, learning and succession to grow people once they're in.

#### Candidate portal

Candidates get their own portal — one-click apply, a "My applications" tracker, job alerts and a talent pool, on a careers page you can serve from your own domain. Pre-hire documents, candidate messaging and data-rights requests are built in.

#### Recruitment agency portal

Offshore recruitment agencies get their own external login — seatless, with no access to your workspace — to see the requisitions you share, submit candidates straight into your ATS with document scans and a field video, and view and download the attested authorization letters. You invite each agency, track visa-processing milestones and handle withdrawals, all in one place.

#### Job descriptions

Versioned job descriptions attached to each job title — read and acknowledged by the holder, with a manager view of who has signed and nudges for who hasn't. An optional AI draft writes the summary, responsibilities and requirements in English or Arabic for HR to review, edit and publish — the AI proposes, it never publishes on its own.

#### Roles & permissions

Custom roles with granular permissions, and a security-scoped IT Admin role that runs the workspace and SSO without ever seeing salary or personal records.

#### Data-access audit log

A transparent record of who read pay data, documents and privacy exports — tenant-visible and toggleable, so you can meet PDPL and GDPR access-transparency obligations.

#### Org structure

Branches, departments, locations and positions — the org chart your headcount, reporting and compliance hang off.

#### Saudi payroll & statutory

GOSI calculated inside every pay run, end-of-service (EOSB) liability and settlements, live Nitaqat and Saudization tracking, and interest-free housing advances and staff loans repaid through payroll — built for the Kingdom.

#### Credentials & renewals

Track Iqama, licence and permit expiry with automatic reminders, and batch-renew documents and credentials when they fall due.

#### Compensation & succession

Manager-led compensation review cycles, establishment positions tracked filled-versus-vacant, succession plans and individual development paths.

#### Recognition & moments

Peer kudos with a points leaderboard, and a birthday and work-anniversary feed to mark the moments that matter.

#### Cases & offboarding

Probation tracking, a disciplinary and violations register, confidential — optionally anonymous — grievance cases, employee self-service data-change requests, and resignation with exit interviews, a cross-department clearance checklist and automatic access cutoff.

#### KSA government workflows

Iqama renewal cycles, exit & re-entry and final-exit visas, and overseas block-visa hiring — with fee pricing, approvals and credential write-back, processed in-house. Government fines import by CSV; FulcrumGrid prepares and records, it never files on your behalf.

#### Total rewards & insurance

Annual total-rewards statements — cash, employer GOSI, benefit share and leave value in one figure — plus medical-insurance membership administration with add, remove, change and renewal-deadline reminders.

#### Data-subject rights

Access and erasure requests (DSAR) backed by a structured retention classification, with a documented legal basis for every record — built for PDPL and GDPR.

#### Posts to your ledger

Draft journal vouchers to SAP Business One or Daftara, and GL posting to FulcrumGrid TMS with reversal reconciliation — HR prepares the entries, your finance system posts them.

#### Developer platform & analytics

A versioned REST API with scoped keys and signed webhooks, OIDC single sign-on and SCIM provisioning and your own custom domain — plus workforce, headcount and engagement dashboards.

03 · Built for

## For the people who look after people.

#### HR & People teams

#### Managers

#### Employees

Self-service for payslips, time off, and personal details — answers without an email to HR.

New · On your phone

## HR Suite in your pocket.

The everyday tasks, on any phone — no app store needed. Open it in your phone's browser and add it to your home screen.

#### Clock in and out

One tap, with an on-site location check, a live shift timer and your week at a glance.

#### Leave & approvals

Request time off on a calendar that knows your weekends and holidays. Managers approve leave, expenses and overtime in one inbox.

#### Pay & documents

Payslips with the full breakdown, expense claims with a photo of the receipt, your documents and your benefits.

Open the app

iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen. Android: menu → Install app. Sign in with your workspace, email and password.

## TMS
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/tms/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Logistics & finance · Available now

# Run your whole logistics operation — and its books — on one grid.

FulcrumGrid TMS is a logistics-operations and finance suite for GCC businesses — freight forwarders, transport and fleet operators, container yards and depots, couriers, and 3PL warehouses. Arabic and English, multi-currency, multi-tenant.

Request a demo All products

01 · Pricing

## Pricing — from SAR 600 / user / mo.

A core Platform + Finance base from SAR 600 per user / month, with operational modules added on as you need them, plus a one-time implementation — talk to sales for a full quote.

#### Platform + Finance base

The core every tenant runs on — the platform itself and a native finance ledger. Everything else is a module you add.

#### Modules you switch on

Forwarding, Transport, Yard, Parcel, Warehousing, Purchasing & Inventory, Workshop, HR & Payroll and Sales are add-on modules — switch each one on as your operation needs it.

Request a demo

02 · Capabilities

## Run the operation and the finance on one system.

Twelve capabilities, from the shipment file to the general ledger.

#### Built-in finance

A native double-entry general ledger with AR, AP, bank reconciliation and job-level P&L, so operations and accounting live on one system.

#### VAT engine & returns

Output, input and import VAT kept as distinct accounts, with VAT-return preparation.

#### Freight forwarding

Shipment files, cargo and containers, transport documents, tariffs and demurrage and detention — with GCC seaports, airports and border crossings built in.

#### Customs clearance

Declarations with customs duty kept separate from import VAT, and claimant records.

#### Transport & fleet

Container and cargo job orders, legs, carriers — your own or a vendor's — and a driver app.

#### Container yard & depot

Gate-in and gate-out, occupancy, zones, multi-yard and storage billing — with a 3D yard view.

#### Parcel & express

Booking, hubs, first and last mile, cash-on-delivery, an SLA clock, a rate engine and tracking.

#### Warehousing & 3PL

Addressable storage, putaway, pick, pack and ship, cycle counts and storage billing.

#### Purchasing & inventory

Purchase orders, goods receipts, stock valuation and invoice matching.

#### Maintenance & workshop

Assets, work orders, preventive maintenance, and parts and labour.

#### ERP connectors

Two-way connectors for SAP Business One, Odoo and Oracle (Fusion and OIC), plus GPS and telematics, SMS, OIDC single sign-on, webhooks and a REST API.

#### Multi-tenant & multi-currency

Strict per-tenant isolation with row-level security, every amount in its own ISO currency, and Arabic and English with full right-to-left.

03 · Built for

## Built for GCC logistics.

#### Freight forwarders

Sea, air and land shipment files, customs clearance, and the finance behind them — in one place.

#### Transport & fleet operators

Container and cargo job orders, legs, carriers and drivers — costed and invoiced as you go.

#### Container yards & depots

Gate moves, occupancy and storage billing across one yard or many, with a 3D view of the yard.

#### Couriers & last-mile

Parcel booking, hubs, first and last mile, cash-on-delivery and an SLA clock, with live tracking.

#### 3PL & warehouses

Addressable storage, putaway, pick, pack and ship, and storage billing per client.

04 · Your region

## Built for the GCC.

Multi-tenant, multi-currency and Arabic-first — TMS works the way the Gulf works.

#### Across the GCC

Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman — one tenant per company, strictly isolated from the next.

#### Multi-currency

Every amount carries its own ISO currency, so you quote, cost and invoice in SAR, AED, USD or any currency your trade lanes use.

#### Arabic & English

Arabic and English throughout, with full right-to-left — for your team and for the documents you issue.

#### VAT, kept straight

Output, input and import VAT held as distinct accounts, with VAT-return preparation for your filings.

05 · Works with the grid

## One ledger across the grid.

TMS is the finance hub of the grid. Run it with your other FulcrumGrid apps and the books stay in one place — no re-keying, no second source of truth.

#### TMS ↔ HR Suite

Payroll, expense and loan journals post straight to the TMS ledger, and posted entries flow back for reconciliation — so people costs and operations stay in step on one set of books.

#### TMS ↔ Collection

Receivables and write-offs post into the TMS ledger, and ageing and reconciliation flow back to Collection — so what you collect and what you owe stay in sync, both ways.

#### TMS → Command Center

Live TMS operations stream to Command Center, so shipments, revenue and exceptions show up on its dashboards and alerts.

06 · The FulcrumGrid family

## Assure
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/assure/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Governance · Available now

# Compliance you can prove.

Assure maps Saudi regulatory obligations to the controls that satisfy them, then drives the evidence end to end — generated on schedule, reviewed by a second pair of eyes, and locked so it holds up to an audit. Governance, risk and compliance, built for Saudi regulation.

Request a demo All products

01 · Pricing

## Pricing — talk to sales.

Assure is self-hosted and priced to your estate — the legal entities you run, the frameworks in scope and the people who use it. Tell us your scope and we'll put a figure to it.

Request a demo Talk to sales

02 · Capabilities

## Governance, risk and compliance in one system.

Every obligation mapped to a control, every control backed by evidence — the whole GRC cycle, tracked and enforced.

#### Saudi regulatory catalog

Obligations arrive pre-mapped for NCA ECC-2, PDPL, CMA Corporate Governance and the Companies Law, alongside ISO 27001 and NIST CSF — applied per legal entity by a scope gate.

#### Multi-entity scope gate

Register every legal entity, and the scope gate decides which obligations apply to each from its attributes — so a group assesses once and applies the result across all its entities.

#### Recurring obligation engine

Compliance tasks are generated automatically on both the Hijri and Gregorian calendars, so nothing lapses between reviews.

#### Maker-checker workflow

Submit, review, approve: every piece of evidence moves through a segregation of duties the database enforces, not just the screen.

#### Immutable evidence vault

Every uploaded file is content-hashed on arrival, so it can't be altered or deleted after the fact.

#### Controls & crosswalk

Rate each control's implementation and maturity, and map one control to several frameworks so the same evidence is reused, not re-collected.

#### Risk register

Score risks inherent and residual, attach treatment plans, and time-box risk acceptance so it auto-reopens when it expires.

#### Authorized attack-surface scanning

Outside-in scanning gated by signed authorization, asset-ownership checks and a kill switch, so security testing stays in scope — findings carry remediation SLAs by severity.

#### Cloud posture (CSPM)

Read-only connections to AWS, Azure and GCP run scheduled cloud-posture checks — no static keys stored — and raise findings against your controls.

#### PDPL privacy toolkit

Handle data-subject requests (DSAR) and keep Records of Processing Activities (RoPA), with DPIA flags where processing needs a closer look.

#### Vendor risk (TPRM)

A third-party register with risk tiers, data-shared flags and a reassessment cadence, so vendor risk stays current.

#### Incident management

Track severity and timeline, with a regulatory-notification deadline clock running from the moment an incident is logged.

#### Attestations

Run sign-off campaigns that collect signatures and issue certificates when each attestation completes.

#### My Work inbox

A personal queue that shows each user exactly the obligations, reviews and attestations awaiting their action — nothing to hunt for.

#### Executive dashboard & KRIs

Board-ready indicators — open critical findings, SLA breaches, overdue obligations, compliance % and open incidents — with posture tracked day over day.

#### Reports & exports

Compliance-status and audit-pack exports to CSV, plus print-ready reports to hand an auditor or the board.

#### Audit-ready & secure

An append-only audit trail, CSV and PDF reports, OIDC single sign-on, API tokens and per-tenant isolation with row-level security — in Arabic and English.

03 · Built for

## For the people who answer to the regulator.

#### Compliance & GRC leads

Own the obligation calendar and the control library, and see at a glance what's covered, what's due and what's overdue.

#### Risk owners

Score and treat risk in one register, with residual ratings and acceptances that don't quietly expire.

#### Security & IT teams

Turn posture findings and incidents into tracked work with deadlines, mapped straight to the controls they affect.

#### Internal audit

Pull the evidence, the crosswalk and the append-only trail you need to test controls and sign off with confidence.

04 · Your region

## Built for Saudi regulation.

Assure's obligation catalog is mapped to the Kingdom's regulators and law, so the controls, the calendar and the evidence all speak to KSA compliance out of the box.

#### Saudi regulators, pre-mapped

Obligations for NCA ECC-2, PDPL, CMA Corporate Governance and the Companies Law arrive already mapped to controls, ready to apply per legal entity.

#### Hijri & Gregorian calendars

The obligation engine runs on both calendars, so recurring duties fall due on the dates your regulators actually use.

#### Arabic & English

The platform works in Arabic and English throughout, so compliance teams and auditors read the same record in their own language.

#### Self-hosted in the Kingdom

Assure is self-hosted, so regulated data can stay inside KSA and inside the infrastructure you already trust.

## Close
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/products/close/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Finance · Available now

# Close the books, with the proof attached.

Close is the calculation layer for your IFRS period-end estimates — IAS 19, IFRS 9 and IFRS 16 — with every input frozen, every assumption evidenced, and every run reproducible down to the hash. A preparer's workspace for Saudi finance teams, built to stand up to an audit.

Request a demo All products

01 · Pricing

## Pricing — talk to sales.

Close has no public price. We scope it to your reporting entities and your close, then quote it.

#### Close

Priced per engagement

Talk to sales —

No published price yet. Tell us how you close and we'll put a number to it.

#### What a demo covers

In one short call

Your period-end estimates ✓

The audit pack and sign-off trail ✓

How a run stays reproducible ✓

Fit for your reporting entities ✓

Request a demo Talk to sales ↗

02 · Capabilities

## IFRS estimates, built to be proven.

Every period-end calculation, from a frozen input to a signed-off audit pack.

#### IFRS period-end engines

IAS 19 end-of-service benefits, IFRS 9 expected credit loss and IFRS 16 leases, in one workspace.

#### Controlled close

Open, review and lock each reporting period; reopening needs a second approver and a logged reason.

#### Frozen input snapshots

Source data is validated and frozen with a content hash, so a later change to the source never alters a past result.

#### Versioned assumptions with evidence

Every discount rate or growth assumption carries a rationale and an attached evidence file, and must be approved before it's used.

#### Reproducible runs

Every calculation re-runs to a byte-identical result hash, provable to an auditor.

#### Segregation of duties

The same person can't both prepare and approve an estimate.

#### External actuary sign-off

IAS 19 runs carry a dedicated actuary review and sign-off stage.

#### Tracked adjustments

Manual overrides are recorded as separate lines with a reason and an approver, never typed over the computed figures.

#### Draft journal vouchers

Balanced, tie-to-results journals exported as CSV or Excel for your ERP.

#### One-click audit pack

A bilingual Excel pack per run — inputs, assumptions, workings, sensitivities and the sign-off trail — with a hash manifest.

#### PDPL-grade access control

Every view, export or download of personal data is gated and written to an append-only access log.

#### Arabic-first, RTL

The whole workspace is built right-to-left, with full Arabic and English and multi-currency (ISO-4217, SAR default).

03 · Built for

## Built for the preparer's chair.

#### Finance teams

Prepare IAS 19, IFRS 9 and IFRS 16 estimates for KSA listed and public-interest companies, ready for review.

#### Group controllers

Consolidate period-end estimates across entities with one lock, one trail and one audit pack.

#### IFRS reporting

Hand your auditor reproducible numbers and a full evidence trail instead of a folder of spreadsheets.

04 · Your region

## Built for Saudi Arabia.

SOCPA-endorsed IFRS, Arabic-first, and multi-currency — Close works the way KSA finance works.

#### SOCPA-endorsed IFRS

Built for the IFRS standards as endorsed by SOCPA for Saudi reporting entities.

#### Arabic-first, right-to-left

The whole workspace runs right-to-left, in full Arabic and English.

#### Multi-currency

Figures carry their own ISO-4217 currency, with SAR as the default.

#### Hands off to your ERP

Draft journal vouchers export as CSV or Excel for SAP Business One or any ledger — Close prepares, your ERP posts.

Finance · Available now

# Every company you run, on one dashboard.

Consolidate pulls the commercial and financial figures out of your accounting system and brings them into one operator dashboard — revenue, cash, receivables, VAT and P&L across every company you run, side by side and rolled up. Connected to Daftra today, with more sources landing behind the same seam.

Request a demo All products

01 · Pricing

Unlimited users · 14-day free trial

Enterprise · 50+ Custom

Connected to Daftra today; more sources on the way.

#### What a demo covers

In one short call

Connecting your Daftra companies ✓

The consolidated KPI dashboard ✓

How snapshots and base-currency roll-up work ✓

Fit for the companies you run ✓

Request a demo Talk to sales ↗

02 · Capabilities

## The whole group, read from the books.

Commercial and financial figures only — no HR — consolidated across every company you connect.

#### One dashboard, every company

Revenue, collections, cash, receivables and payables for each company you run — side by side and consolidated into one view.

#### AR ageing

Open receivables bucketed by age, so you can see what's current and what's slipping — per company and across the group.

#### P&L snapshot

Expenses, other income and a net figure read straight from your books, alongside revenue and cash.

#### VAT & ZATCA status

VAT derived from your invoices and purchases, with each company's ZATCA e-invoicing status surfaced (best-effort).

#### Recurring revenue & pipeline

MRR from subscriptions and an estimates-to-invoices conversion view, where your books carry them.

#### Client insight

Client counts, new-versus-returning cohorts and your top clients by value, drawn from invoice history.

#### Base-currency consolidation

Each company keeps its own currency; you set a base currency and FX rates, and mixed-currency entities roll up into one comparable total.

#### Per-company drill-in

A companies table that opens any single entity's detail — from the group headline down to one company's figures.

#### Nightly snapshots

A worker pulls each company's figures on a schedule; the dashboard reads those snapshots, so it loads fast and never hammers your accounting system live.

#### Encrypted keys, read-only

API keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and never sent back to the browser. Consolidate only reads your figures — it never writes to your books.

#### Hardened connections

Every data pull is host-pinned with SSRF protection, rejected redirects and strict size and time limits, behind an optional operator token.

#### Install it like an app

An installable progressive web app with an offline fallback and opt-in push that tells you when a fresh snapshot is in.

03 · Built for

## Built for the operator's chair.

#### Multi-company owners

See every business you run side by side, without stitching spreadsheets together at month-end.

#### Finance leadership

A consolidated read on revenue, cash, receivables and P&L across the group, refreshed on a schedule.

#### Group controllers

Mixed currencies and entities rolled into one comparable view, each still drillable to its own detail.

04 · Your sources

## Daftra today, more sources next.

Connect a company in Settings with its subdomain and API key — no migration, nothing to install on your side.

#### Daftra — connected

Point Consolidate at your Daftra companies and the commercial and financial figures flow in. Live today.

#### More sources, same seam

SAP Business One, Odoo and Oracle are on the way behind the same connector, so a new source is add-once, not a rebuild.

#### Multi-currency, one base

Entities keep their own currency; set FX to a base currency for the consolidated total, with SAR as the default.

#### Secure by default

Encrypted API keys, host-pinned read-only access and an optional operator token gating the whole dashboard.

#### Cloud

Our managed, multi-tenant cloud — included on every plan, with nothing for you to run or maintain.

A single-tenant instance isolated to your organization, with its own database. Available on Enterprise.

Run FulcrumGrid in your own datacenter or private cloud, behind your firewall. Available on Enterprise, by arrangement.

Choose the region your data is stored and processed in, to meet local requirements.

#### Servers in your region

We run infrastructure in every region we serve, so your data sits on servers close to your users — low latency, and kept in-region.

## Pricing questions, answered.

Each app is billed monthly its own way — flat per organization, per seat, or per workspace. Switch to annual billing to save 20%. You can change plans at any time.

#### Do you offer discounts?

We offer special pricing for nonprofits, educational institutions, and early-stage startups. Reach out and we'll help find the right fit.

# FulcrumGrid vs. spreadsheets

Almost every business starts in a spreadsheet. Here's an honest look at where spreadsheets still work, where they break down, and what a purpose-built app gives you instead.

01 · Side by side

## Side by side.

Spreadsheets · FulcrumGrid

Multiple people at once · Version conflicts and “final_v3” chaos · Real-time, multi-user by design

Access control · All-or-nothing file sharing · Role-based access per person

Audit trail · None — edits are silent · Full history of who changed what

Automation · Manual formulas and copy-paste · Automated reminders and workflows

Reporting · Rebuilt by hand each time · Real-time dashboards and reports

Data integrity · One wrong cell breaks a formula · Structured, validated records

Scaling · Slows and breaks as data grows · Built to grow with you

Your data · Yours, but siloed in files · Yours, and exportable anytime

02 · Honest take

## When a spreadsheet is still the right tool.

Spreadsheets are excellent for quick models, throwaway calculations, and solo one-off analysis — fast, flexible, and familiar. FulcrumGrid isn't trying to replace that. The switch pays off once several people share the file, it becomes the system of record for a process, or a single wrong cell starts costing real money.

03 · FAQ

## Common questions.

#### Is FulcrumGrid a spreadsheet replacement?

For running a business process — invoicing, HR records, operations tracking — yes. FulcrumGrid replaces the fragile spreadsheets teams outgrow with structured, multi-user apps. For quick one-off analysis, a spreadsheet is still a fine tool.

#### Can I import my existing spreadsheets?

Yes. You can bring your records in when you set up an app. Tell us what you have on the contact page and we’ll help you move.

#### When is a spreadsheet still the better choice?

For a quick model, a throwaway calculation, or a solo one-off analysis, a spreadsheet is fast and flexible. The moment several people share it, it becomes a system of record, or mistakes start to cost money, a purpose-built app pays off.

## How to Calculate PTO Accrual: Formulas, Rates & Examples
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/how-to-calculate-pto-accrual/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / How to calculate PTO accrual

HR

# How to Calculate PTO Accrual: Formulas, Rates & Examples

How to calculate PTO accrual step by step — the formula, accrual rates by pay period, hourly vs salaried, and worked examples you can copy. Plus a quick FAQ.

September 9, 2026 · 6 min read

The short answer: to calculate PTO accrual, divide the paid time off an employee earns in a year by the time they work in a year. Per hour worked, that's annual PTO hours ÷ annual work hours . Per paycheck, it's annual PTO hours ÷ number of pay periods . Everything below is just applying that with real numbers.

## What is PTO accrual?

PTO accrual means employees earn their paid time off gradually as they work, rather than receiving the whole year's balance up front. Someone might earn a few hours every paycheck, so by mid-year they've banked roughly half their annual allowance. It's the fairer, more common alternative to a lump-sum grant — especially for hourly staff and new hires.

## The PTO accrual formula

Start with two numbers: how much PTO the employee gets per year, and the period you're accruing over. Then:

Per hour worked: annual PTO hours ÷ annual work hours

Per pay period: annual PTO hours ÷ number of pay periods in the year

A standard full-time year is 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks). Pay periods depend on your schedule: 52 weekly, 26 biweekly, 24 semi-monthly, or 12 monthly.

## How to calculate the accrual rate per hour worked

Use this when PTO should track actual hours — the standard approach for hourly and part-time staff.

Example: a full-time employee gets 10 days (80 hours) of PTO a year.

80 PTO hours ÷ 2,080 work hours = 0.0385 hours of PTO per hour worked

So an 80-hour biweekly paycheck earns 80 × 0.0385 = ~3.08 hours of PTO

A part-timer who worked 50 hours that period earns 50 × 0.0385 = ~1.92 hours

## How to calculate accrual per pay period

Use this for salaried staff, where each paycheck simply adds a fixed amount.

Example: the same 80 hours of annual PTO, paid biweekly (26 periods):

80 ÷ 26 = ~3.08 hours per paycheck

Weekly (52): 80 ÷ 52 = ~1.54 hours

Semi-monthly (24): 80 ÷ 24 = ~3.33 hours

Monthly (12): 80 ÷ 12 = ~6.67 hours

For a more generous 15-day (120-hour) policy, just swap the numerator: 120 ÷ 26 = ~4.62 hours biweekly; 20 days (160 hours) = 160 ÷ 26 = ~6.15 hours.

## Three rules that keep accrual clean

Set a cap or carryover rule. Decide the maximum balance an employee can bank, and whether unused time rolls over, is paid out, or is lost at year-end. Without a cap, balances grow into a real liability.

Decide what hours count. Does PTO accrue on overtime? On other paid leave? Most policies accrue on regular hours only — write it down and apply it consistently.

Round the same way for everyone. Pick a rounding rule (say, to two decimals or the nearest quarter-hour) and use it across the board so no one's balance drifts.

## Frequently asked questions

How many PTO days is two weeks?

For a full-time employee working 8-hour days, two weeks of PTO is 10 working days, or 80 hours. Most companies track PTO in hours rather than days so it works cleanly for part-time and hourly staff too.

How do you calculate a PTO accrual rate per hour worked?

Divide the annual PTO hours by the number of hours worked in a year. For 80 hours (10 days) of PTO and a 2,080-hour work year, that's 80 ÷ 2,080 = 0.0385 hours of PTO earned per hour worked.

What is a typical PTO accrual rate?

Many employers offer 10 to 20 days (80 to 160 hours) of PTO per year, often rising with tenure. On a biweekly schedule that works out to roughly 3.08 to 6.15 hours accrued each pay period.

Does PTO accrue on overtime hours?

That's a policy choice. Many employers accrue PTO only on regular hours up to a set cap and exclude overtime — but you should define it clearly in your policy and apply it the same way for everyone.

The math is simple; keeping every balance right across a whole team, every pay period, is where it gets fiddly. That's what a system is for — accruing automatically, applying your caps and carryover rules, and showing each person their live balance. For the policy decisions behind the numbers, see our guide to building a PTO policy , and if you're setting up people operations from scratch, our employee onboarding checklist and guide to HR software for small businesses cover the rest.

## Accounts Receivable vs Accounts Payable: What's the Difference?
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/accounts-receivable-vs-payable/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / Accounts receivable vs accounts payable

Collection

# Accounts Receivable vs Accounts Payable: What's the Difference?

A plain-English guide to accounts receivable vs accounts payable — what each means, how they hit your balance sheet and cash flow, and how to manage both.

September 15, 2026 · 6 min read

If you run a business, two ledgers quietly decide whether you have cash in the bank: what customers owe you, and what you owe everyone else. Those are accounts receivable and accounts payable. They sound like accounting jargon, but understanding the difference — and managing both deliberately — is the heart of healthy cash flow.

## What is accounts receivable?

Accounts receivable (AR) is money your customers owe you for goods or services you have already delivered but have not been paid for yet. It shows up on your balance sheet as a current asset , because it is cash you expect to collect soon. Every unpaid invoice you have sent is part of your AR.

## What is accounts payable?

Accounts payable (AP) is the mirror image: money you owe to suppliers and vendors for things you have received but not yet paid for. It is a current liability on your balance sheet. Every bill sitting in your inbox waiting to be paid is part of your AP.

## The key difference, in one line

AR is money coming in; AP is money going out. AR is an asset you collect; AP is a liability you settle. One invoice can be both at once — it is AR for the business that sent it and AP for the business that received it.

## How they affect your cash flow

Cash flow lives in the timing gap between the two. If your customers pay you on Net 60 but your suppliers expect Net 15, you are financing that 45-day gap out of your own pocket. Managing AR (collecting faster) and AP (paying on your own terms, without being late) is how you keep the gap from squeezing you. Two useful measures: DSO (days sales outstanding) tracks how fast you collect AR; DPO (days payable outstanding) tracks how long you take to pay AP.

## How to manage both well

Invoice promptly and clearly , with due dates and payment links — the faster an invoice goes out, the faster it comes back.

Track AR by age so you know what is overdue and chase it on a set cadence.

Schedule AP so you pay on time — protecting supplier relationships and any early-pay discounts — without paying early for no reason.

Reconcile both regularly so your books reflect reality, not last month's guess.

## Frequently asked questions

Is accounts receivable an asset or a liability?

Accounts receivable is a current asset. It represents money owed to your business that you expect to collect, usually within a year, so it counts toward what your business owns.

Is accounts payable a debit or a credit?

Accounts payable is a liability, so it normally carries a credit balance. It increases with a credit when you record a new bill and decreases with a debit when you pay it.

Can something be both AR and AP?

Not for the same company on the same transaction, but a single invoice is AR for the seller and AP for the buyer. If you both buy from and sell to the same partner, you may carry AR and AP with them at the same time.

Collecting AR faster is a discipline of its own — see our guides to accounts receivable best practices , reducing days sales outstanding , and choosing invoice payment terms .

## Gross Pay vs Net Pay: What's the Difference?
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/gross-pay-vs-net-pay/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / Gross pay vs net pay

HR

# Gross Pay vs Net Pay: What's the Difference?

A clear explanation of gross pay vs net pay — what each includes, what gets deducted in between, and how to calculate take-home pay.

September 14, 2026 · 5 min read

Every payslip tells two stories: the salary you agreed to, and the amount that actually reaches the employee's bank account. Those are gross pay and net pay, and the gap between them is where taxes, contributions, and deductions live. Getting the difference right matters for budgeting, for payroll, and for every "why is my pay less than my offer?" conversation.

## What is gross pay?

Gross pay is the full amount an employee earns before any deductions . For a salaried worker it is the annual salary divided across pay periods; for an hourly worker it is hours worked times the hourly rate, plus any overtime, bonuses, or allowances. It is the headline number in an offer letter.

## What is net pay?

Net pay — often called take-home pay — is what is left after every deduction comes out of gross pay. It is the number that actually lands in the bank. Net pay is always less than or equal to gross pay.

## What gets deducted in between?

The deductions that turn gross into net vary by country, but usually include:

Income tax or withholding , where it applies.

Social insurance or pension contributions — for example, GOSI in Saudi Arabia.

Employee benefit contributions — health insurance, retirement, and similar.

Voluntary or court-ordered deductions , such as loan repayments.

Some of these are the employee's share; employers often pay an additional share on top that never appears in the employee's gross.

## How to calculate net pay

Start with gross pay, then subtract each deduction in the order your local rules require. In simple terms: Net pay = Gross pay − total deductions. The detail is in knowing which deductions apply, what each rate is, and which are capped — which is exactly why payroll is worth automating rather than doing by hand each month.

## Why the difference matters

For employees, it is the difference between the offer and the reality — worth explaining clearly at hiring. For employers, gross pay plus the employer's own contributions is the true cost of employment, which is usually higher than the salary figure alone. Budget on total cost, communicate on net pay, and keep the calculation transparent on every payslip.

## Frequently asked questions

Is gross pay or net pay higher?

Gross pay is always higher, or equal. Net pay is gross pay minus deductions, so it can never exceed gross pay.

Does gross pay include overtime and bonuses?

Yes. Gross pay is total earnings for the period, including base pay plus any overtime, bonuses, commissions, and taxable allowances, before deductions.

What is the difference between an employee's net pay and the employer's cost?

Net pay is what the employee receives. The employer's cost is gross pay plus the employer's own contributions, such as its share of social insurance, so total employment cost is higher than both gross and net pay.

Pay sits alongside the rest of people operations — see our guides to employee time tracking , calculating PTO accrual , and choosing HR software .

## What Is an Employee Handbook? (And What to Put in It)
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/employee-handbook/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / What is an employee handbook?

HR

# What Is an Employee Handbook? (And What to Put in It)

What an employee handbook is, why every business needs one, and a section-by-section list of what to include — from policies to culture.

September 13, 2026 · 6 min read

An employee handbook is the single place your team can go to learn how your company works — the rules, the benefits, the expectations, and the tone. Done well, it prevents a thousand small questions and protects both the business and its people. Done badly, or not at all, it leaves everyone guessing. Here is what a handbook is and what belongs in one.

## What is an employee handbook?

An employee handbook is a document that sets out your company's policies, procedures, benefits, and expectations for employees. It is part reference manual, part culture statement: it tells people both what they must do (rules and compliance) and how you do things (values and norms). It is usually given at onboarding and updated as the company grows.

## Why every business needs one

A handbook creates consistency — the same rules for everyone — and a written record of the policies you have communicated, which matters if a dispute ever arises. It speeds up onboarding, reduces repetitive questions to HR, and sets expectations clearly so managers are not inventing answers on the spot. Even a small team benefits from writing it down.

## What to include

A practical handbook usually covers:

Welcome and culture — mission, values, and how you work.

Employment basics — contracts, probation, working hours, and attendance.

Pay and benefits — payroll schedule, leave, health cover, and any allowances.

Leave and time off — annual leave, sick leave, and how to request it.

Conduct and expectations — code of conduct, communication, and the disciplinary process.

Health, safety, and security — workplace safety and data / IT policies.

Anti-discrimination and grievances — how issues are raised and handled.

Exit — notice periods and offboarding.

## What to leave out

Keep individual contract terms (specific salaries), fast-changing operational detail, and anything better handled case by case out of the handbook — they date quickly and make it heavier than it needs to be. Link to living documents instead of pasting them in.

## Keeping it current

A handbook is only useful if it is accurate. Review it at least once a year and whenever the law or a major policy changes, version it so people know what is current, and record that each employee has read and acknowledged it. A stale handbook that contradicts practice is worse than none.

## Frequently asked questions

Is an employee handbook legally required?

In most places a handbook itself is not legally required, but many of the individual policies it contains may be — and having them written down helps you stay compliant and consistent. Check the rules where you operate.

What is the difference between an employee handbook and an employment contract?

A contract is a binding agreement with one employee covering their specific terms. A handbook is a general reference of company-wide policies and culture that applies to everyone; it usually is not a contract in itself.

How often should you update an employee handbook?

At least once a year, and immediately whenever a law changes or you introduce or revise a major policy. Version each update and have employees acknowledge the current one.

A handbook pairs naturally with a strong start — see our employee onboarding checklist , building a PTO policy , and writing SOPs your team follows .

## KPIs vs OKRs: What's the Difference and When to Use Each
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/kpis-vs-okrs/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / KPIs vs OKRs

Operations

# KPIs vs OKRs: What's the Difference and When to Use Each

KPIs vs OKRs explained — what each one is, how they differ, and when to use metrics to monitor health versus goals to drive change.

September 12, 2026 · 6 min read

KPIs and OKRs are two of the most-used — and most-confused — acronyms in business. They are not rivals; they answer different questions. KPIs tell you whether the business is healthy right now. OKRs tell you what you are trying to change next. Use the wrong one for the job and you either drift without direction or chase goals while the basics slip.

## What is a KPI?

A KPI — key performance indicator — is a metric that tracks the ongoing health of something that matters: monthly revenue, churn rate, on-time delivery, average response time. KPIs are usually steady measures you monitor continuously against a target or threshold. A good KPI answers, "Is this part of the business performing as it should?"

## What is an OKR?

An OKR — objective and key results — is a goal-setting framework. The Objective is a qualitative, ambitious goal ("make onboarding effortless"); the Key Results are two to five measurable outcomes that prove you hit it ("cut time-to-first-value to under a day," "raise activation to 60%"). OKRs are set for a period — usually a quarter — and are meant to stretch you.

## The key differences

Purpose: KPIs monitor health; OKRs drive change.

Timeframe: KPIs run continuously; OKRs are set per cycle.

Ambition: KPIs should stay in a healthy range; OKRs are meant to be a stretch.

Nature: a KPI is a single metric; an OKR is a goal plus the metrics that prove it.

## How they work together

The best operators use both. KPIs are the dashboard you watch to keep the business running; OKRs are the projects you take on to move it forward. Often a KPI that is drifting becomes the reason for an OKR ("churn is creeping up — this quarter's objective is to fix retention"), and a Key Result is frequently just a target on an existing KPI. Monitor with KPIs; improve with OKRs.

## When to use each

Reach for KPIs when you need to keep a steady eye on performance and catch problems early. Reach for OKRs when you want to rally the team around a small number of ambitious goals for the quarter. If everything is a KPI, nothing changes; if everything is an OKR, the day-to-day slips. Balance the two.

## Frequently asked questions

Can a key result be a KPI?

Yes — very often it is. A Key Result is usually a target on a metric, and that metric may already be a KPI you track. The difference is that the KPI runs continuously while the Key Result is a specific target for the OKR cycle.

Are OKRs better than KPIs?

Neither is better; they do different jobs. KPIs monitor ongoing health, OKRs drive focused change. Most teams need both.

How many KPIs and OKRs should you have?

Keep both few. A handful of KPIs per team keeps the dashboard readable, and one to three objectives with two to five key results each per quarter keeps focus. Too many of either dilutes attention.

Both live or die on the numbers you choose to watch — see our guides to what to track in an operations dashboard and running a weekly operations review .

← Back to the blog

## What Is Dunning? How the Dunning Process Works
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/what-is-dunning/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / What is dunning?

Collection

# What Is Dunning? How the Dunning Process Works

What dunning means, how a dunning process works, and how to build a polite, effective sequence that collects overdue invoices without losing customers.

September 11, 2026 · 6 min read

"Dunning" is an old word for a modern problem: getting paid for invoices that have gone past due. A dunning process is simply the structured, repeatable way a business follows up on overdue payments — the sequence of reminders that turns "we'll pay soon" into money in the account. Done with a system, it collects more and strains fewer relationships.

## What does "dunning" mean?

Dunning is the process of communicating with customers to collect money they owe on overdue invoices. A "dunning notice" or "dunning letter" is one of those reminders. The term is old, but the idea is everyday accounts-receivable work: following up, consistently and politely, until an invoice is paid.

## How the dunning process works

A dunning process is a planned sequence of reminders that escalate gently over time. A typical flow:

Before due date — a friendly heads-up that payment is coming up.

On the due date — a simple "it's due today" note with a payment link.

A few days overdue — a polite reminder that the invoice is now past due.

Further overdue — a firmer message referencing your terms and any late fee.

Final notice — a clear statement of next steps before escalation.

Each step keeps the same clarity: which invoice, how much, and a one-click way to pay.

## Automated vs manual dunning

Manual dunning — chasing each invoice by hand — works until you have more than a handful of customers, then it slips. Automated dunning sends the right message at the right interval on its own, so nothing falls through the cracks and no one has to remember to follow up. Automation also keeps the tone consistent and the timing disciplined, which is exactly what collects.

## How to dun without damaging relationships

Stay polite early. Most late payment is an oversight, not a refusal — assume good faith at first.

Be specific. Every message should name the invoice, amount, due date, and payment link.

Escalate on a schedule , not on emotion — consistency reads as professional, not aggressive.

Make paying trivially easy — a payment link beats "please remit to…" every time.

## When dunning is not enough

If a full sequence passes with no response and no dialogue, it is time to escalate — a phone call, a payment plan, pausing further work, or, as a last resort, a formal collections or legal route. A good dunning process makes this rare by catching most late payers early and giving them an easy way to pay.

## Frequently asked questions

What is a dunning notice?

A dunning notice is a reminder sent to a customer about an overdue invoice. It states which invoice is unpaid, the amount, and how to pay, and it is usually one step in a larger dunning sequence that escalates over time.

What is the difference between dunning and collections?

Dunning is the routine, in-house process of reminding customers about overdue invoices. Collections usually refers to a later, more formal stage — often involving a dedicated team or an outside agency — once normal reminders have failed.

How many dunning reminders should you send?

There is no fixed number, but a common sequence is four to five messages — a pre-due reminder, a due-date note, and two or three escalating follow-ups — ending with a clear final notice before you escalate further.

Dunning is one piece of getting paid on time — see our guides to writing payment reminder emails , accounts receivable best practices , and reducing days sales outstanding .

## Employee Time Tracking: A Practical Guide
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/employee-time-tracking/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / Employee time tracking

HR

# Employee Time Tracking: A Practical Guide

How to track employee time without micromanaging — methods, what to log, overtime rules, and how it ties into payroll and PTO.

September 7, 2026 · 6 min read

Time tracking has a trust problem before it even starts: employees hear "we're tracking your hours" and think surveillance, while managers hear "we need accurate time data" and think payroll and billing accuracy. Both are right, and the gap between them closes the moment tracking is built around a clear, stated purpose instead of vague oversight.

## Decide why you're tracking time — it changes everything else

The right approach depends entirely on what the data is for. Payroll accuracy for hourly staff needs precise clock-in/clock-out records. Client billing needs time tied to a project or task, not just a total for the day. Capacity planning needs a rough sense of where hours go, not minute-by-minute logs. Pick the wrong method for your actual purpose and you'll either collect too little detail to be useful or so much that nobody keeps it up.

## The three common methods

Clock in/out — a timestamp at the start and end of a shift. Simple, standard for hourly and shift-based roles, and usually a legal requirement where minimum-wage or overtime rules apply.

Timesheets — hours logged against projects, clients, or tasks, usually filled in daily or weekly. Best when the "why" is billing or project costing, since it captures where time went, not just how much there was.

Automatic tracking — software that detects activity or app usage in the background. Highest detail, highest trust cost — use it deliberately and disclose it, or skip it for a lighter method.

Most small teams don't need the heaviest option. Match the method to the decision the data will actually inform.

## What to actually log

Keep the record itself simple: who, what date, start and end time (or total hours), and — if billing or costing matters — which project or client. Resist the urge to capture more "just in case." Extra fields that don't map to a real use tend to go unfilled, which quietly undermines trust in the whole system once people notice the data is incomplete anyway.

## Overtime rules need to be explicit, not assumed

Define, in writing, what counts as overtime — hours beyond a daily or weekly threshold — and whether it requires pre-approval. A policy that exists only as "management's discretion" produces disputes precisely when they're most expensive: after the extra hours have already been worked. State the threshold, the rate, and the approval process before anyone needs to use them.

## Connect it to payroll and PTO, not a separate system

Time data that lives apart from payroll gets re-entered, mistyped, and disputed. When tracked hours flow directly into pay calculations — and when PTO balances are visible in the same place as worked hours — an employee can see one accurate picture instead of reconciling two systems that occasionally disagree about how much they actually worked or have left.

## Keeping it from feeling like surveillance

Tell people why — a stated purpose ("this feeds payroll and client invoices") reads very differently from silence.

Track work, not people — log hours and tasks, not screenshots or keystroke counts, unless there's a specific, disclosed reason.

Make the data visible to the employee too — a one-way system that only managers can see breeds more suspicion than one everyone can check.

Time tracking works best as part of the same system that already runs onboarding and PTO, not a separate tool bolted on top. If you're setting this up alongside a new hire's first weeks, pair it with our employee onboarding checklist , and see our guide to choosing HR software for a small business for what to look for in a system that ties time, PTO, and payroll together.

## Performance Review Questions: A Manager's Template
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/performance-review-questions/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / Performance review questions

HR

# Performance Review Questions: A Manager's Template

Ready-to-use performance review questions for managers — self-review, manager, and 1:1 growth questions, plus how to run a review that's fair and useful.

September 7, 2026 · 7 min read

A performance review is only as good as the questions behind it. Ask vague ones and you get a box-ticking exercise nobody values; ask sharp, specific ones and you get an honest conversation that actually helps someone grow. Below is a template you can copy — organised into the three parts of a good review: the employee's self-review, the manager's assessment, and a forward-looking growth conversation.

## Before you start: three ground rules

No surprises. A review should summarise feedback the person has already heard through the year, not spring it on them. If something is new, that's a coaching failure, not a review moment.

Specific over general. "Great communicator" helps no one. "Your launch note gave three teams what they needed in one place" is feedback someone can build on.

Balance backward and forward. Half the review is what happened; half is what's next. Don't let it become only a grade.

## 1. Self-review questions (send these first)

Have the employee answer these a few days ahead — it sets the agenda and surfaces gaps between how they and you see the period.

What are you most proud of since the last review, and why?

Which goals did you meet, and which fell short — what got in the way?

Where did you grow a skill or take on something new?

What part of your role energises you most? What drains you?

Where do you want to develop next, and what support would help?

## 2. Manager assessment questions (your prep)

Answer these for yourself, backed by specific examples and notes from the period — not just the last few weeks.

Did they deliver on the goals we agreed? Where did they exceed or miss, and why?

What's the single strongest example of their impact this period?

Where is the one most valuable area to improve — and is it a skill, a habit, or a resourcing issue?

How do they work with the team — do they make those around them better?

Are they in the right role and scope for where they're headed?

## 3. Growth & forward-looking questions (the conversation)

What do you want to be doing 12 months from now — and what's the first step?

What are the two or three priorities that matter most next quarter?

What can I do differently as your manager to help you do your best work?

Is anything getting in your way that we haven't talked about?

What does success look like for you — beyond just hitting targets?

## Rating scales: keep them simple

If you use ratings, a 3- or 5-point scale with clear definitions beats a vague 1–10. Whatever you pick, anchor each level in behaviour ("consistently exceeds," "meets," "developing") and apply it the same way for everyone — consistency is what makes a scale fair.

Good questions are step one; running reviews the same way for everyone — on a schedule, with a record you can look back on — is what makes them fair and useful over time. That's easier when reviews, goals, and history live in one system rather than scattered documents. It also builds on the fundamentals we cover in our employee onboarding checklist and PTO policy guide — and if you're still choosing a system to run it all, our guide to HR software for small businesses covers what to look for.

## Invoice Payment Terms Explained (Net 30, 2/10 Net 30 & More)
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/invoice-payment-terms/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / Invoice payment terms explained

Collection

# Invoice Payment Terms Explained (Net 30, 2/10 Net 30 & More)

A plain-English guide to invoice payment terms — Net 30, Net 15, due on receipt, EOM, 2/10 Net 30 early-payment discounts, and deposits — and how to choose the right ones.

September 1, 2026 · 7 min read

Payment terms are the quiet agreement that decides when you get paid — and they matter as much to your cash flow as the price itself. Set them clearly and you get predictable income; leave them vague and you get slow payers, disputes, and awkward chases. This guide explains the common terms in plain English and how to choose the ones that fit your business.

## What "payment terms" actually means

Payment terms are the conditions you set for getting paid: how long the customer has, when the clock starts, which methods you accept, and any discount or penalty attached. They belong on the invoice — but ideally they're agreed before the work starts, so nothing is a surprise.

## The common terms, decoded

Due on receipt — payment is expected as soon as the invoice arrives. Best for one-off jobs or new customers.

Net 7 / Net 15 / Net 30 / Net 60 — payment is due that many days after the invoice date. Net 30 is the most common in B2B; shorter terms (Net 7–15) pull cash in faster.

EOM (end of month) — due at the end of the month the invoice was issued. "Net 30 EOM" means 30 days after month-end.

CIA / PIA — "cash in advance" / "payment in advance." The full amount is paid before you deliver. Common for custom or high-risk work.

Deposit / 50% upfront — part paid before work begins, the balance on completion. Protects you on larger projects.

Milestone billing — payment tied to stages of delivery, so cash arrives as the work progresses.

Retainer — a recurring fixed amount, billed ahead, for ongoing work.

## Early-payment discounts: "2/10 Net 30"

This is the one that confuses people. 2/10 Net 30 means: the full amount is due in 30 days, but if the customer pays within 10 days, they take a 2% discount. It's a tool to pull cash in sooner. Just weigh the cost — offering 2% to be paid 20 days early is a real discount, so use it where faster cash is worth more than the margin.

## Start the clock on the right date

"Net 30" is meaningless if no one agrees what day zero is. Make it explicit: is it 30 days from the invoice date , the delivery date , or receipt of the invoice? Better still, state the actual due date ("Due: October 1, 2026") on the invoice. Specific dates get paid; relative terms get interpreted.

## How to choose your terms

Match your own cash cycle. If you pay suppliers on Net 15, collecting on Net 60 quietly finances your customers.

Shorter for new or risky customers , more generous for trusted, high-value ones.

Add a late-payment policy (a fee or interest) and state it up front — then apply it consistently.

Make paying effortless — accepted methods and a payment link on every invoice.

Good terms only help if they're actually collected. The habits that turn terms into on-time cash — clear invoices, a reminder cadence, and a tight collection process — are covered in our guides to writing payment reminder emails , accounts receivable best practices , and reducing days sales outstanding .

## How to Write SOPs Your Team Actually Follows
URL: https://fulcrumgrid.com/blog/sop-guide-small-business/
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Home / Blog / How to write SOPs your team follows

Operations

# How to Write SOPs Your Team Actually Follows

A practical guide to writing standard operating procedures your team will actually use — format, review cadence, ownership, and common mistakes to avoid.

September 1, 2026 · 6 min read

Most standard operating procedures fail for the same reason: someone wrote a long, careful document once, and nobody has opened it since. It sits in a shared drive while the actual process lives in one person's head, gets re-explained to every new hire from scratch, and drifts a little further from what's written down every month.

An SOP that gets used isn't longer or more thorough than one that doesn't — it's built differently from the start. Here's what that looks like.

## 1. Write it as steps, not prose

A paragraph describing a process is something people read once and forget. A numbered list of specific actions is something people can follow mid-task without re-reading the whole thing. Each step should be a single action with a clear outcome — "Export the report" not "Handle the reporting process." If a step needs a decision, name the decision explicitly rather than assuming it's obvious.

## 2. Give every SOP one owner

An SOP with no named owner slowly goes stale, because nobody feels responsible for noticing when it no longer matches reality. Assign one person per procedure whose job includes keeping it current — not necessarily the person who does the task most often, but someone with the standing to update it when the process changes.

## 3. Put it where the work actually happens

A procedure buried three folders deep in a shared drive might as well not exist. The SOP for a task needs to be reachable in the moment someone is doing that task — linked from the tool they're using, not filed separately from it. If people have to go looking for it, they'll ask a colleague instead, and the document stops being the source of truth.

## 4. Set a review cadence, not a one-time write-up

Processes change faster than documentation does, unless documentation review is scheduled rather than incidental. A simple rule works well: every SOP gets reviewed on a fixed cadence (quarterly for anything customer-facing or compliance-related, twice a year for the rest), and whoever last touched the underlying process is responsible for flagging it if something changed in between.

## 5. Test it on someone who's never done the task

The person who wrote an SOP is the worst judge of whether it's clear, because they already know what it's supposed to say. Before treating a procedure as finished, hand it to someone unfamiliar with the task and watch where they hesitate or get it wrong. Every point of confusion is a gap in the document, not a gap in the reader.

## Common mistakes that quietly kill adoption

Writing for compliance, not for use. A procedure written to satisfy an audit checklist and a procedure written to actually guide someone through a task read very differently — and only one of them gets opened voluntarily.

No version control. If people can't tell whether they're looking at the current version, they'll stop trusting it and go back to asking around.

Too much detail, too soon. Cover the 80% of cases that happen every time first. Edge cases can live in a linked appendix instead of burying the main flow.

SOPs work best when they're tied to the systems people already use for the task, not maintained as a separate exercise. That's easier when the underlying process — approvals, alerts, reporting — already runs through one operations dashboard instead of being scattered across tools. It pairs naturally with getting the right metrics in front of the team in the first place, and with a clean onboarding process for handing procedures to new hires.
